card.name: Dhalo
card.tagline: Goan women's nocturnal ritual dance of protection
card.profile: Dhalo is a ritual folk dance of Goa performed exclusively by women as a prayer for the protection and prosperity of their households (Wikipedia). Conducted over roughly a week in the lunar month of Pausha at the onset of winter, 12-24 women dance in two parallel rows facing each other with interlocked arms, at a slower pace than the energetic Fugdi (Wikipedia). Songs are sung in Konkani or Marathi on religious and social themes and the dance is performed at a sacred open ground called the 'mand'; on the final day women dress elaborately and draw caricatures of men (Wikipedia; Gomantak Times).
card.insight: Performed by Kunbi, Bhandari, Naik, Gabit and Gaudi communities, Dhalo functions as a living archive of Goan oral tradition - its 'oviyos' preserve folklore and devotional songs, traditionally said to descend from love songs Radha sang to Krishna (Wikipedia; ItsGoa).
